extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists and fiction writers (including agented authors and those seeking representation)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft and career advice for fiction writers aiming to write compelling, market-ready novels and sustain a publishing career. Emphasizes story-level craft (tension, revision, inspiration) plus professional behaviors with agents/publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story quality over external factors
rubrics_metrics.description: What will make you successful isn’t your publisher, agent, deals, promo or blog. It’s your stories, period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the strength of your stories above relying on publishers, agents, marketing, or online presence. Success stems from the work itself; invest time and craft into making the story excellent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-by-line (micro) tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak line-by-line tension in their manuscripts. What makes any type of novel a gripping read is micro-tension that doesn’t let up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure micro-tension on the sentence/paragraph level so readers remain engaged continuously; avoid lapses that relax the reader's emotional investment. Treat each line as an opportunity to raise stakes, question, or forward motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build time to play and explore during revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts should have built into them not just a revision framework, but time to play and explore. So many published novels achieve less than they could. Consequently, readers aren’t as engrossed as they could be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow revision periods for experimentation and discovery rather than strictly mechanical edits. Giving yourself 'play' time can deepen the novel and increase reader engrossment; advocate for this time in professional agreements when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional attitude in author–agent relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: A professional attitude goes a long way. Frustrations happen but pour them into your fiction!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professionalism with agents and industry contacts; manage frustrations constructively and use emotional energy productively (e.g., channel into writing) rather than burning bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use emotional/frustration energy as creative fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Frustrations happen but pour them into your fiction!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transform negative emotions and career frustrations into story material or motivation to improve craft. This turns obstacles into productive creative input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read great fiction for inspiration and craft calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: The adrenaline jolt of reading great fiction is what inspires me to keep going.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly read outstanding fiction to renew passion, learn techniques implicitly, and calibrate your sense of what great writing feels like. Let exemplary works inform your standards and ambitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be bold and innovative despite market caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The devastating impact of the economic downturn... has made our industry fearful and cautious just when it needs to be bold and innovative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a conservative publishing market, strive for boldness and innovation in concept, voice, or execution to stand out. Recognize market headwinds but prioritize originality where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career focus: sustained productivity and building a body of work
rubrics_metrics.description: Still here after 30 years, my agency selling 150 titles per year. Writing the Breakout Novel is rated by many writers among the classics in this field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term success ties to consistent output, building a recognizable body of work, and producing titles that endure; treat career development as part of the craft (e.g., produce, learn, publish repeatedly).
